title: Sticky Breadcrumb Timeline & Span Mini-Summary for Trace Drilldown
creator: Amira Khan
description:
Problem: Users investigating high-latency or cost spikes need a lighter-weight, persistent navigation aid in the request drilldown that keeps context as they pan/zoom a long span timeline. Current trace inspector forces repeated searches and loses correlation context when jumping between spans.

Goal: Design and prototype a sticky breadcrumb timeline + per-span mini-summary that: (1) persistently shows the request path and correlation ids, (2) surfaces actionable quick actions (copy correlation id, jump to parent/next sibling, pin span to dashboard), and (3) displays a compact cost/latency summary for each focused span without requiring full span-detail fetch. The component should be responsive and degrade gracefully for very large/multi-service traces.
acceptance_criteria: Sticky breadcrumb rail exists at the top of trace drilldown and updates as user scrubs timeline
Hover or tap on a breadcrumb reveals span mini-summary card with: span name, service, start/end time, duration, estimated token cost, correlation id with copy action, and quick actions
Mini-summary renders within 150ms for traces with up to 200 spans in the UI; for larger traces it shows an aggregated cluster row
Filter builder supports quick filter from breadcrumb (e.g., add filter: service = 'router' and duration > 50ms)
Design prototype vetted by Eng and PM with performance constraints documented and handoff specs in Figma
design_decisions: Use a horizontal sticky rail instead of a persistent vertical sidebar to preserve vertical space for long timelines
Mini-summary fetch will use a slim telemetry endpoint that returns aggregated fields (no full logs) to meet 150ms render target
For traces >200 spans, show aggregated cluster breadcrumbs ("3 spans collapsed") with ability to expand on demand to avoid overfetching
Include token-cost estimator in UI based on model, prompt length heuristics and per-token unit cost pulled from Cost API; make it opt-out in settings for customers who don't track cost
Quick actions wired to existing runtime routes: copy correlation id to clipboard, open related request in new tab, and pin span to dashboard via dashboard API
comments: 2025-02-19 - Priya Patel: +1 on rail vs sidebar. Concern: mobile breakpoint — we should collapse to a single badge with 'open rail' affordance.

2025-03-03 - Design review notes (Amira): Dev feedback says KV cache doesn't expose per-span token counts; we'll estimate using model & tokenization heuristics and mark estimates as 'approx.' in UI
